samples.summary: MemDocStore.batch(): an adopted checkpoint that the body materialized and then reverted is never popped, leaving a dead undo entry while the pre-batch redo stack is restored underneath it
samples.evidence: In `batch()`'s `finally`, `wroteNothing` is true whenever the body's net effect is nothing. The pop is gated on `if (!adopted)`, so for the `snapshot(); batch{write; revert}` shape (the ordering `TextEditor.withUndoUnit` now uses everywhere) the checkpoint that `willWrite()` already pushed onto `undoStack` stays there, and `this.redoStack = priorRedo` (line 341) puts back the redo entries that `willWrite()` deliberately cleared. Net result: one dead Cmd+Z that changes nothing, followed by a redo stack that now sits one press further away — exactly the symptom the `snapshot()` deferral was introduced to remove (see the comment at lines 244-252). The comment at lines 297-300 explicitly claims this shape is treated as free ("`priorRedo` still puts it back for a body that writes and then reverts itself, which `wroteNothing` also treats as free"), which the `!adopted` guard contradicts. Reachable through FindReplaceState.replaceActive/replaceAll with a replacement equal to the match, and through any batched toolbar action whose writes cancel out.

samples.summary: canUndo()'s "floor dropped" latch is keyed on a hard-coded copy of the SDK's undo cap; if the real cap is smaller than 50 the latch never fires and the #1045 over-restriction persists
samples.evidence: `YORKIE_MAX_UNDO_DEPTH = 50` duplicates the SDK's unexported `MaxUndoRedoStackDepth`. The mark-not-found branch only latches when `stack.length >= 50`. If the SDK's real cap is *below* 50 (a version bump, a differently configured build), entries start shifting off at a stack length the condition never reaches, so every subsequent `canUndo()` falls through to `stack.length > this.undoFloorDepth` with a floor depth that can no longer be refreshed (the mark is gone) — i.e. undo silently stops one press early per dropped entry, which is the exact defect this change exists to fix. The SDK is not vendored in the tree, so the constant cannot be verified here; nothing in CI pins it either.

samples.summary: revocableDocStore's `get` trap omits the non-configurable/non-writable own-property escape hatch that readOnlyDocStore's `get` carries, so such a property would make every read through the handle throw a TypeError
samples.evidence: `readOnlyDocStore.get` (lines 84-87) explicitly returns `own.value` for an own property with `configurable === false && writable === false`, because a proxy may not report anything else for one — and its three refusing traps make the same exception. `revocableDocStore.get` (lines 196-205) returns a *bound wrapper* for any function-valued property and the raw value otherwise, with no such check, while its `getOwnPropertyDescriptor`/`ownKeys`/`has` traps forward to `readOnlyDocStore` once revoked. If either store ever gains a frozen own member (e.g. `Object.defineProperty(this, 'x', {writable:false, configurable:false})`), reading it through `getStore()`/`getDoc()`'s handle becomes a hard TypeError rather than a no-op. No store has such a property today, so this is contained — but the two wrappers now disagree about a rule the older one documents as load-bearing.

samples.summary: writePageSetup still writes through the raw `docStore`, the one hole the diff closed in guardedSetPageSetup
samples.evidence: The diff changed `guardedSetPageSetup` to `revocableStore.setPageSetup(...)` with the comment "writing to the raw store here would be the single page-setup-shaped hole left in a disposed handle", but `writePageSetup` (line 2360) — the other page-setup write path, reached from `EditorAPI.setPageSetup` and from `ruler.onMarginChange` — still calls `docStore.setPageSetup(...)` directly. Currently unreachable after dispose (`setPageSetup` is in `MUTATING_METHODS` and `ruler.dispose()` detaches its handlers at packages/docs/src/view/ruler/index.ts:460), so this is an inconsistency rather than a live hole; it becomes one if the allowlist ever drifts.
